differences.title: 1. PERFORMANCE
differences.leftDesc: FastAPI leverages Python's async capabilities and Starlette for high concurrency, offering excellent performance for I/O-bound tasks, but limited by GIL for CPU-bound operations.
differences.rightDesc: Axum, built on Rust's Tokio runtime, offers near-zero-cost abstractions and fearless concurrency without a GIL, resulting in raw performance and efficient resource utilization.

differences.title: 2. TYPE SAFETY
differences.leftDesc: FastAPI uses Pydantic for runtime data validation, catching errors when requests are processed. Type hints improve readability but don't prevent all runtime type issues.
differences.rightDesc: Axum, leveraging Rust's strong type system, enforces type safety at compile time, eliminating entire classes of runtime errors and ensuring data integrity proactively.

differences.title: 3. CONCURRENCY MODEL
differences.leftDesc: FastAPI uses Python's asyncio for asynchronous operations. Concurrency is limited by the Global Interpreter Lock (GIL) for CPU-bound tasks, affecting true parallelism.
differences.rightDesc: Axum utilizes Rust's ownership and borrowing system with Tokio's async runtime, enabling safe, fine-grained concurrency and true parallelism across CPU cores without a GIL.

differences.title: 4. ECOSYSTEM & LIBRARIES
differences.leftDesc: FastAPI benefits from Python's extensive libraries for data science, machine learning, and general-purpose programming, offering a mature and diverse set of tools.
differences.rightDesc: Axum leverages the rapidly expanding Rust ecosystem, focusing on systems programming and web development. It integrates well with other Rust crates for robust applications.

differences.title: 5. MEMORY MANAGEMENT
differences.leftDesc: Python's garbage collector manages memory automatically, which can introduce overhead and pauses. FastAPI inherits this behavior from the Python runtime.
differences.rightDesc: Rust's memory safety is achieved through its ownership system and borrow checker at compile time, offering deterministic performance without garbage collection overhead.

differences.title: 6. DEVELOPMENT SPEED
differences.leftDesc: FastAPI's Python syntax and automatic OpenAPI/Swagger UI generation enable very fast initial development and prototyping, ideal for quick iteration.
differences.rightDesc: Axum's strictness and compile-time checks can lead to a slightly slower initial ramp-up but result in more stable, maintainable codebases and fewer runtime surprises.

differences.title: 7. ERROR HANDLING
differences.leftDesc: FastAPI handles errors primarily through Python's exception handling mechanisms, with validation errors surfaced via Pydantic during request processing.
differences.rightDesc: Axum leverages Rust's `Result` and `Option` types for explicit error handling, ensuring errors are addressed at compile time rather than encountered at runtime.
